- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizons.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.3) — add 2–5% to forecast for 3–5 day horizons.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — cap forecast increases after 2 consecutive high sentiment days.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, penalize early overshoots — if forecast > 15% above 18-day moving average, subtract 1–2% per day for next 5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope by 30–50% for remaining days.
- Avoid forecasting downward trends when sentiment remains > 0.6 — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to prevent premature sell-off.
